---
title: "Exercise 4.8"
---


## Solution
**Claim.**
There exists countable subset $A \subset F$ such that $\bar{A}=F$.

**Proof.**
If $F = \emptyset$, then let $A=\emptyset$. Suppose, therefore, that $F \neq \emptyset$. 

For each pair $p,q\in\mathbb Q$ with $p<q$ and
$$ (p,q)\cap F\neq\varnothing,$$
choose one point
$$ a_{p,q}\in(p,q)\cap F.$$

Let
$$A=\{a_{p,q} : p,q\in\mathbb Q,\ p<q,\ (p,q)\cap F\neq\varnothing \}.$$

Since $\mathbb Q^2$ is countable, $A$ is also countable. And by construction, $A \subset F$.
Moreover, since $F$ is closed,
$$ \overline A\subset F.$$

To prove the reverse inclusion, let $x\in F$ and let $\epsilon>0$. 
By the density of $\mathbb Q$ in $\mathbb R$, we can choose $p,q\in\mathbb Q$ such that
$$x-\epsilon<p<x<q<x+\epsilon.$$

Since $(p,q) \cap F \neq \emptyset$, this intersection is nonempty. Hence there exists. 
Hence, there exists 
$$a_{p,q} \in A$$. 
It follows that
$$ \vert x - a_{p,q}\vert < \epsilon.$$
Thus every neighborhood of $x$ intersects $A$, so
$$ x\in\overline A.$$
Therefore, $F\subset\overline A.$

Hence, $\overline A=F.$  $\blacksquare$

<br>

We now construct the desired measure.

If $F=\varnothing$, define
$$\nu(B)=0$$
for every Borel set $B\subset[0,1]$. Then $\nu$ is a finite measure whose support is $\varnothing$.

Now suppose that $F\neq\varnothing$. Since $A$ is countable, we may write
$$ A=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\} $$
if $A$ is infinite, or
$$ A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_N\} $$
if $A$ is finite.

Assign to each $a_i$ a positive weight $w_i$ such that
$$\sum_i w_i<\infty.$$
For example, if $A$ is infinite, take
$$w_i=\frac1{2^i},$$
and if $A$ has $N$ elements, take
$$w_i=\frac{1}{N}.$$

Define, for every Borel set $B\subset[0,1]$,
$$\nu(B) = \sum_{\{i:a_i \in  B \}} w_i.$$

Thus $\nu$ is a measure, and
$$\nu([0,1])=\sum_i w_i<\infty.$$
Hence $\nu$ is finite. Moreover, since $A\subset F$,
$$\nu(F^c)=0.$$

It remains to show that $F$ is the smallest closed set with this property. 
Let $G\subset[0,1]$ be closed and suppose that
$$\nu(G^c)=0.$$
Since every $w_i$ is positive, no point $a_i$ can belong to $G^c$. Hence
$$ A\subset G. $$
Since $G$ is closed,
$$ F=\overline A\subset G. $$

Therefore, $F$ is the smallest closed set $G$ such that
$$\nu(G^c)=0.$$
Thus the support of $\nu$ is $F$.
